1 نَكَثَ , (S, K,) aor.
نَكُثَ , (K, Msb,) and
نَكِثَ , (K,) inf. n. نَكْثٌ, (TA,) He undid [the threads of] a garment of the kind called كِسَاء, &c.: (Msb:) he undid, or untwisted, a rope. (S, K.) ―
-b2- نَكَثَ السِّوَاكَ, aor.
نَكُثَ , inf. n. نَكْثٌ; He, or it, made the head of the tooth-stick to be uncompacted, disintegrated, disunited, or seperated, in its fibres: and so the verb signifies with respect to other things. (TA.) [See also 8.] ―
-b3- نَكَثَ, (aor.
نَكُثَ , and
نَكِثَ , K, inf. n. نَكْثٌ, TA,) (tropical:) He dissolved, violated, or broke, a covenant, or compact, (S, K,) or an act of inauguration, &c. (TA.) ―
-b4- نَكَثَ عَنِ الأَمْرِ i. q. نَكَصَ (Aboo-Turáb, in TA, art. نكص.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
